title: The own checker on CaDiCaL and on Bitwuzla given the engine's word-level terms: five workloads, full checks (Phase 6c, part 2)
description: Phase 6c of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md (the native stream), its second part: Bitwuzla on word-level terms for the workloads where the formula's size dominates. The prototype is JVMCONTRACT_SOLVER=bitwuzla-words: the solver interface gains Terms (lib/src/bmc/sat.rs), and over a solver that takes terms the engine's encoding (lib/src/bmc/bits.rs) builds no circuits. Each gate is defined to Bitwuzla as a Boolean term, and each addition, subtraction, multiplication, signed division and remainder, comparison, shift by a symbolic amount, bitwise operation of two non-constant values and ite of two values as one bit-vector term (bvadd, bvsdiv, bvult, ite, ...), whose result bits are extracts of it (lib/src/bmc/bitwuzla.rs). Constants fold as before, and nothing is left to the engine's lazy division and multiplication: the solver is given the operation itself. Arrays stay the engine's bounded cells, read and written through ites over the index (no array theory). lib/solvers/compare.py --words runs the own checker's full checks of the benchmark's five workloads (real/midpoint/search-within-bound, the bounded binary search; example/141; example/142; held/reverse; held/prefix-sums) under strict, with the benchmark's own command lines (lib/benchmark/run.py, imported, not changed), three times each on three solvers: the bundled CaDiCaL 1.9.5 (the baseline, on the same machine), bitwuzla-words with Bitwuzla 0.8.2's defaults (sat-solver cadical, produce-models), and bitwuzla-words with preprocess=0. Bitwuzla is loaded with dlopen from ~/tools/bitwuzla/current, the install job 20261106-194049 made on this runner. There are no transcripts: the solver isn't given clauses. The script writes lib/solvers/comparison/word-level.json (every run, with each check's word-level operation count, the solvers' signatures, the library's path and sha256, the commit, the machine) and word-level.md (the table). It fails if CaDiCaL misses a case's expected verdict, if any decisive verdict is wrong, or if the solvers' decisive verdicts differ; a Bitwuzla run out of time is a measurement, listed as not decided. The bit-blasted part is job 20261106-224616. Times are taken on a shared runner, so other jobs may run beside it. No network.
expected: exits 0: all five cases verified on CaDiCaL, every decisive verdict on bitwuzla-words verified; word-level.json and word-level.md written with the three solvers' signatures

resources.notes: Measured inline on this machine, one run each: reverse 0.18 s on CaDiCaL and 0.12 s on bitwuzla-words, prefix sums 0.05 and 0.06 s, example 141 2.35 s on bitwuzla-words (CaDiCaL about 2.2 s); peak 73 MB. The five checks on CaDiCaL take 8.3 s together, so three runs on three solvers come to a few minutes unless a case runs out of time on Bitwuzla (600 s each at most); the build is a few minutes.

steps.name: Bitwuzla loads here, and the word-level operations are the JVM's on it
steps.run: cd lib && out=$(cargo test --release --lib bitwuzla -- --nocapture 2>&1); status=$?; echo "$out"; test $status -eq 0 && ! grep -q "skipped:" <<< "$out"
